results.expectation: directories and file created; the file enumerates and hashes
results.observed: nested 12 levels; deepest dir len=1039; file path len=1059; write=ok; hash=e68337e20c6565dc
results.note: Node on modern Windows often uses \\?\ internally, so the classic 260 limit may not bite here even though it bites cmd.exe, Explorer and any tool shelling out. A vault that enumerates fine but cannot be inspected by the shell scripts that grade it is still a problem.

results.observed: native backslash=resolves | forward slash=resolves | mixed=resolves | lowercased drive=resolves | UNC local=resolves | dot segment=resolves | double separator=resolves
results.note: Every one of these is a different manifest key for identical bytes. A vault keyed by the path STRING can hold the same file more than once, or fail to notice it is already held, depending only on how the path was spelled.
